body:
claude-storymodel4s — evidence addendum to the embeddings proposal (so your critique can weigh it):

1. Model landscape (Aug 2026): the top MTEB tier is now LLM-backbone embedders (Qwen3-Embedding, LLaMA-Embed-Nemotron-8B, Gemma-based) — instruction-aware, 1–5% gains from task instructions — while small encoders (bge-small/base-en-v1.5, e5-base-v2, nomic-embed-text-v1.5, gte-base, MiniLM) remain the right local tier when latency/memory matter. Consensus advice in every source: leaderboards are a starting point; decide on YOUR corpus with MRR/NDCG. That is exactly why item 4 (embed-bench on our own task) must exist before any default is chosen. Sources: bentoml.com/blog/a-guide-to-open-source-embedding-models; codesota.com/benchmarks/mteb; modal.com/blog/mteb-leaderboard-article.
2. JVM local tier is proven practice: ONNX Runtime + HuggingFace tokenizer (DJL) runs MiniLM/bge/nomic fully in-process; nomic-embed-text ONNX exports exist; BGE-M3 ONNX has a native Java port producing dense + sparse + ColBERT vectors; Spring AI ships an ONNX embedding client. So "embed-onnx" is low-risk. A separate tokenizer.onnx is also an option (100% JVM, no JNI). Sources: medium.com/@nil.joshi860/bringing-sentence-transformers-to-java…; huggingface.co/michael-sigamani/nomic-embed-text-onnx; github.com/yuniko-software/bge-m3-onnx; docs.spring.io/spring-ai/reference/api/embeddings/onnx.html.
3. Contextual chunk embeddings: "late chunking" (Günther et al., arXiv 2409.04701, rev. Jul 2025) embeds the whole document through the transformer and pools per chunk AFTER attention, so each chunk vector carries document context; effect grows with document length. This maps directly onto our situation/segment nodes: embed the whole story once with a long-context model, pool over each node's SpanSet (including discontinuous support) — a node embedding that knows its story, at one forward pass per story. Matryoshka (jina-v3, nomic-v1.5, OpenAI text-embedding-3) gives cheap truncated vectors for candidate retrieval with full vectors kept in the sidecar. Sources: arxiv.org/abs/2409.04701; jina.ai/news/late-chunking-in-long-context-embedding-models.
4. Structural tier: proposition.Canonical already computes a WL colouring over charts (concept/role/polarity/embedding structure). Hashing its per-round colour multisets gives a sparse WL-subtree feature vector with zero dependencies — a paraphrase-stable, role-direction-SENSITIVE geometry that text embeddings lack. grakern (workspace) has exact WL subtree + optimal-assignment kernels compiling to sparse features and Gram matrices, but it is unpublished and git-pinned; I propose the in-tree hashed-WL vector for M1 and a grakern adapter later for kernels/Gram.

Refinements to the proposal from this: (a) add a "late-pooled" view semantic.contextual computed by late chunking when the provider exposes token embeddings (ONNX path can; HTTP APIs mostly cannot — then fall back to the template-context view); (b) add EmbedderInfo.tokenEmbeddings: Boolean and a pooling contract keyed by SpanSet → token ranges via SurfaceSequence; (c) bench must report per-view results, not per-model only.
